items.followUp: What is a truth value in Boolean logic?

rubric.why: A Boolean proposition is a statement.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying a proposition as a statement.

rubric.why: A Boolean proposition has one of two truth values.
rubric.description: States that it is either true or false.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for giving both possible truth values.

modelAnswer: A Boolean proposition is a statement that has a truth value.
It is either true or false, but not both.

items.followUp: Differentiate between data privacy and data confidentiality.

rubric.why: Privacy concerns control over personal information.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining that privacy concerns control or rights over personal data.

rubric.why: Confidentiality protects information from access by unauthorized people.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that only authorized people should access the data.

modelAnswer: Data privacy is a person's control over how their personal data is collected and used.
Data confidentiality means protecting data so that only authorized people can access it.

items.followUp: What does a router do when it receives a data packet?

rubric.why: Routing involves selecting a path for data.
rubric.description: Mentions the selection of a route or path.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that a route or path is selected.

rubric.why: The route carries data from its source toward its destination.
rubric.description: Identifies the packet's journey to its destination.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for connecting routing with forwarding data toward its destination.

modelAnswer: The routing process is the selection of a path for data packets to travel through a network.
It moves packets from their source toward their destination, often using routers.

items.followUp: Which protocol is used to send and receive email?

rubric.why: FTP stands for File Transfer Protocol and is used for transferring files.
rubric.description: Identifies file transfer as FTP's purpose.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that FTP transfers files.

rubric.why: FTP transfers files between computers over a network.
rubric.description: States where or between what FTP transfers files.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for mentioning transfer between computers over a network or the Internet.

modelAnswer: File Transfer Protocol (FTP) is used to transfer files between computers.
It transfers files over a network such as the Internet.

items.followUp: What is the World Wide Web?

rubric.why: The Internet is a global network of interconnected networks.
rubric.description: Identifies the Internet as a global network.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing it as a global or interconnected network.

rubric.why: The Internet connects computers and devices and uses communication protocols such as TCP/IP.
rubric.description: Mentions connected computers/devices or the protocols used.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for mentioning connected computers/devices or TCP/IP.

modelAnswer: The Internet is a worldwide system of interconnected computer networks.
It enables computers and other devices to communicate using standard protocols such as TCP/IP.

items.followUp: How many bits are in an IPv4 address?

rubric.why: An IPv6 address has a length of 128 bits.
IPv6 addresses are written as hexadecimal groups separated by colons.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for mentioning hexadecimal groups or colon separators.

modelAnswer: An IPv6 address is a 128-bit address used to identify a device on a network.
It is written as eight groups of hexadecimal digits separated by colons.

items.followUp: What is the difference between a paired tag and an unpaired tag in HTML?

rubric.why: One type is paired (also called a container tag).
rubric.description: Names the first type of HTML tag.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming paired or container tags.

rubric.why: The other type is unpaired (also called an empty tag).
rubric.description: Names the second type of HTML tag.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming unpaired or empty tags.

modelAnswer: The two types of HTML tags are paired (container) tags and unpaired (empty) tags.
